**Answer: n = 799**

**Digit sums of blocks.** Let S(n) be the sum of all digits from 1 to n.

- From 0 to 99, each of the two lower positions cycles through 0–9 ten times per block of ten, so the tens and units digits contribute 2 × 10 × 45 = 900. Hence S(99) = 900.
- For a block of numbers 100h to 100h + 99 (h = 1, …, 9), the hundreds digit h appears 100 times, contributing 100h. The last two digits contribute another 900. So each block adds 100h + 900.

**Cumulative totals.**

| Block | Added | Running total |
|---|---|---|
| 1–99 | — | 900 |
| 100–199 | 1000 | 1900 |
| 200–299 | 1100 | 3000 |
| 300–399 | 1200 | 4200 |
| 400–499 | 1300 | 5500 |
| 500–599 | 1400 | 6900 |
| 600–699 | 1500 | 8400 |
| 700–799 | 1600 | 10000 |

The sum reaches exactly 10,000 at the end of the 700–799 block, so n = 799.

ANSWER: 799
